It was introduced to provide a categorical distribution over the latent space, contrasting with the continuous Gaussian distributions of standard VAEs [S1].

The claim states that the model was introduced to provide a categorical distribution over the latent space, contrasting with the continuous Gaussian distributions of standard VAEs. Source [S1] explicitly states: 'Codebook model is a VQ-VAE [49,54], which is a variational autoencoder with a categorical distribution over the latent space.' This confirms the first part of the claim. While the text does not explicitly mention 'continuous Gaussian distributions of standard VAEs' in the provided snippets, the definition of VQ-VAE as a VAE with a categorical distribution inherently contrasts with the standard VAE formulation (which uses continuous latent variables, typically Gaussian). Since the core fact—that the model uses a categorical distribution over the latent space—is directly supported by the text, and this is the defining characteristic distinguishing it from standard VAEs, the claim is supported.
